question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To keep one’s temper
solution:
The correct answer is: **To remain calm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To keep one's temper"** means to remain calm and not become angry, even in a stressful situation. (शांत रहना)

 
 
• **Example:** Despite the provocation, he managed to keep his temper and responded politely.
 
 
 
• **"To remain calm"** refers to maintaining a composed and tranquil state of mind without showing agitation or anger. (शांत रहना)
 
 
• **Example:** During the crisis, she remained calm and handled the situation effectively.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To meet with disaster** (आपदा का सामना करना): To encounter a catastrophic event or situation.

 
 
• **Example:** The team met with disaster when their project failed just before the deadline.
 
 
 
• **To become impatient** (अधीर होना): To become restless or eager due to delay or frustration.
 
 
• **Example:** He became impatient while waiting for the slow internet connection to load the page.
 
 
 
• **To become angry** (गुस्सा होना): To feel or show strong annoyance or displeasure.
 
 
• **Example:** She became angry when she found out that her brother had broken her favorite vase.
